behavior: Privy key rotation never breaks sign-in: the api verifies tokens with the JWKS key named by their kid
acceptance: At startup the api loads the ES256 keys from PRIVY_JWKS_URL and verifies each token with the key named by its kid; tokens signed by any published key pass, and every F046 rejection still answers 401
An unknown kid refetches the keys at most once per minute, then 401; a known kid makes no network call; a failed fetch at startup stops the api with an error; PRIVY_VERIFICATION_KEY is no longer read
notes: 2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: BLOCKING: apps/backend/internal/auth/auth.go:99 runs the shared JWKS refetch with the request context (httpapi/auth.go:21 passes r.Context()). fetchedAt is set first (auth.go:96), so a client that sends any ES256 token with an unknown kid and hangs up aborts the fetch and spends the once-per-minute slot. Repeating this each minute keeps the api from ever loading a rotated key: unauthenticated, breaks R-29. Even a normal client disconnect gives a minute of 401s for the new key. Reproduced in a scratch copy: an httptest api, a JWKS that answers in 300 ms, an attacker request with a 50 ms timeout, then a token from the rotated key gets 401. With fetch(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) the same test passes (the http.Client 10 s timeout still bounds it). Add a test for this. Non-blocking: auth.go:149-155 one malformed EC key fails the whole fetch instead of being skipped; auth.go:156 duplicate kid keeps the last; requests with the new kid that arrive during an in-flight refetch get 401; no test that a failed refetch keeps the old keys. Checked OK: alg check runs before keyfunc in golang-jwt v5.3.1, so none/HS256 never reach a fetch; the key set holds only *ecdsa.PublicKey; a missing kid tries only published keys (safe); 200 concurrent mixed requests under -race give exactly 1 refetch; 1 MiB body limit, status check, point check; the real Privy JWKS (2 EC P-256 ES256 sig keys) loads and the api starts; a refused JWKS URL stops the api with exit 1 and no secret in the log. pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test passes.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Re-review of af7992d. The earlier blocker is fixed: auth.go:100 now fetches with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), so a caller that hangs up can no longer abort the shared refetch and waste the once-per-minute slot. The http.Client 10 s timeout in cmd/api still bounds the fetch. New TestRefetchSurvivesACancelledRequest (auth_test.go:118) fails when the fix is reverted and passes with it. My scratch PoC (httptest api, JWKS that answers in 300 ms, attacker hangs up after 50 ms, then a token from the rotated key) now gets 200; with the fix reverted it gets 401. Non-blocking, unchanged from the first review: auth.go:149-155 one malformed EC key fails the whole fetch (fails safe); auth.go:156 duplicate kid keeps the last; a new-kid request that arrives during a running refetch gets 401; no test that a failed refetch keeps the old keys. auth_test.go:123-128 signs the same token twice (the cancelled call could reuse token). Still OK: alg check before keyfunc (golang-jwt v5.3.1), keyset holds only *ecdsa.PublicKey, a missing kid tries only published keys, 1 refetch under 200 concurrent requests with -race, the real Privy JWKS loads and the api starts, a failed startup fetch stops the api without printing secrets. pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test passes.

proof.1: backend: TestVerifyUsesTheKeyNamedByKid: with two published keys, tokens signed by either (kid set) and a token without kid pass, a kid naming the other key fails; TestOnlyValidPrivyTokensPass (httpapi, now over a JWKS) keeps every F046 rejection at 401; the real api loaded Privy's JWKS at startup
proof.2: backend: TestUnknownKidRefetchesAtMostOncePerMinute (fake clock: no fetch within a minute, one fetch after, rotated key then passes, 5 unknown kids in a minute cause no fetch); TestRefetchSurvivesACancelledRequest (a hung-up caller can't abort the shared refetch); TestVerifyUsesTheKeyNamedByKid counts 1 fetch for known kids; TestVerificationMakesNoNetworkCall; TestNewVerifierNeedsKeys; config reads PRIVY_JWKS_URL, not PRIVY_VERIFICATION_KEY
